messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — cutover window today 18:00 UTC for the Python/TS SDKs. Intend to ship python 2.1.0 and @redwood/sdk 2.1.0. Canaries ran in staging this morning.
ben: 👍 What's the pin policy for clients? Are we pinning examples and quickstarts to 2.0.x or switching them to 2.1.0 immediately?
carla: Suggest pinning quickstarts to 2.0.x for 48h, update docs to show `pip install redwood-sdk==2.0.4` and `npm i @redwood/sdk@2.0.4` to avoid surprise for new signups.
dan: For the npm package we'll publish 2.1.0 with a deprecation note for legacy sync client. Add a BREAKING-MIGRATION section in the changelog.
erin: QA checklist: smoketests, streaming sample, function-calling example, and cookiecutter template. I have a test run queued.
release-bot: release pipeline triggered for python: redwood-sdk 2.1.0, npm: @redwood/sdk 2.1.0. Canary group: 5% prod, 100% staging. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/releases/1771004821
ci-bot: build artifacts uploaded: pywheel: sdist & wheel, npm tgz published to internal registry. Checks: unit ✅, lint ✅, integration (staging) running.
alice: Plan: 18:00 cutover, publish to public registries at 18:05, update docs site at 18:10, pin examples to 2.0.4 in a follow-up PR. Rollback plan if we see errors: revert npm tag and unpublish py wheel, restore routes to 2.0.x.
ben: If we need to rollback, can we do a fast pin on our CDN examples? I can push a quick PR to lock the examples in <10m.
carla: I'll prepare the deprecation notice text for the sync client — short blurb + migration snippet. Put it in the release notes so support can paste it.
erin: QA run finished: staging smoketests passed, streaming perf within expected range, minor warnings on one TS typing edge-case (non-blocking).
release-bot: 18:00 UTC — starting staged rollout to production canary (5%).
ci-bot: canary deploy completed. Observability links: latency dashboard http://dash/latency/1771004821, error-rate http://dash/errors/1771004821
ben: @alice monitoring live traffic now. Adding a temporary rate-limit threshold in case of regen storms.
dan: Pushing npm @redwood/sdk@2.1.0 to public registry in 2m.
alice: ok publish at will once you see canary stable for 5m. Docs update queued: #docs/512
release-bot: public publish complete: npm @redwood/sdk@2.1.0, pip redwood-sdk==2.1.0. Changelog published at https://docs.redwood.ai/changelog/2.1.0
carla: deprecation blurb added to release notes and docs. Support playbook updated.
ben: Found a consumer error in logs — traceback in streaming adapter when `stop_sequence` is present. Error rate bumped to 0.6% over baseline.
erin: Reproduced locally. It's a regression from the new streaming backpressure path. Marking severity P2 but noisy for a few customers.
alice: Decision call: rollforward patch or rollback full release? Can we patch and hotfix quickly?
dan: Patch involves touching the runtime stream handler; hotfix build + publish will take ~45m end-to-end. Rollback npm/pypi and CDN pin is ~10-15m.
ben: Given customer impact, prefer rollback to 2.0.4 for now and re-release with fix.
carla: Agree — rollback. I'll post notice to mailing list and support with templated message.
release-bot: initiating rollback procedure: deprecate tag 2.1.0, re-tag stable -> 2.0.4, mark 2.1.0 as yanked in internal registry.
ci-bot: npm unpublish blocked due to policy; performing `npm dist-tag` reassign and publish 2.0.4 as latest. pip: pushing 2.0.4 wheel as latest and yanking 2.1.0 from our internal index.
alice: Ben, push the examples pin PR now. Carla, send support note. Erin, continue root-cause triage and prepare patch PR targeting main.
ben: PR created: #devex/532 pin examples to 2.0.4, deploy in 8m.
carla: Support note sent. Slack template + email to enterprise customers who got early 2.1.0.
erin: Patch PR opened: streaming-backpressure-fix, tests added. CI green locally, requesting review.
ci-bot: rollback complete: npm latest points to 2.0.4, public pip shows 2.0.4 as recommended. Metrics returning to baseline.
alice: Thanks all. We'll keep 2.1.0 branch frozen until fix merges and we run a slower canary next week. Follow-up actions: postmortem if >30min customer impact, bump QA gating for streaming changes, and update our release checklist to include a streaming smoke test.
dan: Will schedule a maintenance canary 1% next Thu after fix merge.
carla: I'll add the deprecation schedule to the roadmap: planned removal of legacy sync client in 30 days, but we'll hold if rollback blocks removal.
ben: TL;DR: rolled 2.1.0 back due to streaming regression, pinned examples to 2.0.4, patch PR opened. Will reattempt release after fix + extended canary.
alice: Good work. Closing thread — I'll create a short release note update in the #releases channel once we have the patch timeline.
